summary: The v39 recording prefixes the wizard Genesis command with a count. C carries that count into read.c:create_particular_parse(), which uses 1 + gm.multi as the requested mimic population; cmd.c:rhack() dispatches wiz_genesis once and clears the count after ECMD_OK. JavaScript rejects the selected wizgenesis row at rhack’s generic counted nonmovement-command boundary before the prompt. Allow this already-ported counted handler through that guard so Genesis consumes the count and clears it in source order.

source.branch: For the input count before C-g, parse() stores the count in gm.multi and spends the initial dispatch by decrementing it once (cmd.c:5142-5144). The C-g binding selects wiz_genesis (cmd.c:1961-1962); rhack() executes that handler while the positive remainder is intact, and its successful ECMD_OK result calls reset_cmd_vars(), clearing gm.multi before allmain.c:moveloop_core() can repeat the command (cmd.c:3810-3816). wiz_genesis() calls create_particular(); read.c:create_particular_parse() initializes d.quan to 1 + gm.multi (read.c:3144-3150), so the count is consumed as population size. The missing behavior is JavaScript cmd.js:rhack()’s fail-closed preflight for counted nonmovement commands, which does not exempt the already-ported wizgenesis row.
callers: cmd.c:parse() at 5142-5146 supplies the counted C-g command key; cmd.c:1961-1962 maps C-g to wiz_genesis().

wizcmds.c:wiz_genesis() at 203-215 calls read.c:create_particular(); read.c:create_particular_parse() at 3144-3150 turns the remaining gm.multi into a monster quantity before create_particular_creation() selects each monster with mkclass().
dependencies: The existing JavaScript wiz_genesis() and read.js:create_particular_parse()/create_particular_creation() are wired and retain the count quantity; only cmd.js:rhack() rejects this counted dispatch.
